docs.title: Mrunmoy Jena
docs.text:
Title: "Spectroscopy of \(\pmb{{}^{24}O}\) and \(\pmb{{}^{22}O}\) via \(\pmb{{}^{25}F(p,2p)}\) quasi-free scattering at R3B Experiment"

Abstract

Quasi-free proton and neutron-knockout reactions in inverse kinematics offer valuable insight into the structure of nuclei far from stability, and the kinematically complete R3B setup (Reactions with Relativistic Radioactive Beams) is ideally suited to study these reactions. The \({}^{25}F(p,2p) {}^{24}O\) reaction probes how a single proton extends the neutron drip line from \(Z=8\), where it ends at \({}^{24}O\), to \(Z=9\) — where the ground-state overlap of \({}^{25}F\) with \({}^{24}O\) turns out to be surprisingly small, and its structural origin remains debated. Since the excited states of \({}^{24}O\) are neutron-unbound, they are reconstructed through their \({}^{23}O + n\) and \({}^{22}O + 2n\) decay channels.

This talk presents the ongoing analysis, focusing on energy reconstruction with the CALIFA calorimeter and, in particular, on the \({}^{22}O + 2n + \gamma\) channel. From Doppler-corrected \(\gamma\)-ray spectra, the populations of the low-lying \({}^{22}O\) states are extracted using simulated response functions, and a \(\gamma\)-multiplicity analysis is developed to separate direct population of the \(2^{+}\) state from cascade feeding.

Cake: Roman Sergei

01.07.2026

docs.title: Lena Kirchner, Anil Adigüzel
docs.text:
Title: "(baby)HYPER"

Abstract

HYPER (Single-\(\lambda\) Hypernuclei Factory) is a pioneering experiment at CERN’s Antimatter Factory designed to produce and discover approximately 200 new single-\(\lambda\) hypernuclei using low-energy antiprotons from the ELENA ring. By capturing antiprotons onto nuclei, HYPER aims to perform high-resolution spectroscopy to measure ground-state binding energies and lifetimes, providing critical data to constrain \(\lambda\)-nucleon and λNN interactions and address the "hyperon puzzle" in neutron star physics. The experiment relies on a compact, multi-purpose detector — utilizing advanced ALICE ITS3 65 nm CMOS technology for its pion tracker — capable of distinguishing weak-decay events from prompt annihilation backgrounds through picosecond timing.

The second part of the talk is about babyHYPER, a dedicated testbed operated during a test beam campaign at the TELMAX beamline at AD. It was designed to prototype key technical solutions for HYPER and to study particle tracking with MAPS detectors in a realistic setup. The testbed consists of a vacuum vessel with vacuum separation and two detector arms, each equipped with three sensors. This configuration allows the performance of the cooling and vacuum systems to be investigated while providing tracking information for vertex reconstruction at the target. The presentation will discuss the vessel design, the role of vacuum separation, and results from sensor cooling, vacuum performance, and tracking analysis.

24.06.2026

docs.title: Henrik Fribert
docs.text:
Title: "New femtoscopic constraints on the ΣN interaction from pp collisions at \(\pmb{\sqrt{s} =}\)13.6 TeV with ALICE"

Abstract

The properties of dense astrophysical objects, such as neutron stars, are governed by the equation of state of nuclear matter. At the extreme baryon densities reached in their cores, hyperons are expected to appear as energetically favorable degrees of freedom. Constraining hyperon-nucleon interactions is therefore essential for accurate astrophysical modeling. However, in the case of the ΣN interaction, the experimental information is scarce.

In this talk, unprecedented precision results on Σ⁻p correlations measured by ALICE in pp collisions at \(\sqrt{s} = 13.6\) TeV during the LHC Run 3 are presented. These measurements are made possible thanks to the excellent tracking capabilities of the new Inner Tracking System, which allows the reconstruction of charged Σ hyperons via their decay to a neutral particle and a charged daughter, identified by the characteristic kink topology of the decay.

The measured correlation functions provide direct access to the strong interaction effects, enabling comparisons with different theoretical interaction potentials. These new results complement the previous Σ⁺p femtoscopic measurements performed by ALICE in Run 2, and pave the way for improved constraints on the strength and isospin dependence of the ΣN interaction, offering essential insights for the equation of state of dense nuclear matter.

Cake: Louna

17.06.2026

docs.title: Davide Cremese
docs.text:
Title: "Probing the initial-state geometry with the Lee-Yang zeros"

Abstract

In relativistic heavy-ion collisions, anisotropic flow provides insights into the collective behavior of the quark-gluon plasma. The Lee-Yang zero method provides a robust framework for anisotropic flow analysis, suppressing non-flow effects through the interparticle correlation between a large number of particles. While this method utilizes the first zero of a generating function in order to isolate collective flow effects, the information that additional zeros may hold remains unexplored. This talk focuses on the application of the second Lee-Yang zero as a complementary observable in the context of flow measurements. Using simulated Pb-Pb collision data generated with the Trento model, we analyze its sensitivity to initial-state parameters and compare its performance to the standard first-zero approach and the established multi-particle correlation method.

Cake: Valentina

10.06.2026

docs.title: Rafael Manhart
docs.text:
Title: "ALICE femtoscopic studies involving pions in Run 2/3 & the connection to NS and axions"

Abstract

The composition of the innermost region of neutron stars remains unknown, and the potential presence of QCD axions has been recently suggested. The properties of axions under high baryonic densities can be related to the in-medium characteristics of pions, which can be studied in pp collisions at the LHC. The emission of multiple hadrons helps mimic high densities because their production distances are short (∼ fm). This talk presents ALICE Run 2 & Run 3 measurements of the pion-proton interaction using femtoscopy in pp collisions at \(\sqrt{s} = 13\) TeV & \(\sqrt{s} = 13.6\) TeV. Using three-body femtoscopy, we report the first measurement of \(p\)–\(p\)–\(\pi\) correlations in the ongoing Run 3 data-taking period, enabling the study of effects beyond pairwise interactions. This offers a distinctive opportunity to study axions and their impact on the equation of state of neutron stars.

03.06.2026

docs.title: Lukas Lautner, Philipp Mann
docs.text:
Title: "ALICE 3 Outer Tracker Cooling Studies"

Abstract

The ALICE collaboration has proposed a completely new apparatus, ALICE 3, for the LHC Run 5. The detector consists of a large tracking system based on Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors (MAPS), complemented by multiple systems for particle identification. The tracking system is divided into Inner and Outer Tracker. With \(32m^2\), just the four barrel layers of the Outer Tracker will constitute the largest MAPS-based detector ever built and will require modularization and industrialization of its production. The combined power consumption of the roughly 45000 individual sensors will exceed 10 kW and require dedicated cooling. Keeping modularity in mind, air cooling is the preferred option. Ongoing R&D work is focused on identifying the optimal cooling solution for the Outer Tracker. For this purpose, we built and continuously upgrade a cooling setup at TUM. To adequately simulate the heat load dummy heater modules are employed and continuously developed to more closely match operational conditions.

We report on the upgrade of the setup, present results showing the feasibility of air cooling the Outer Tracker Barrel and first estimates for the required services.

27.05.2026

docs.title: Wioleta Rzesa
docs.text:
Title: "Probing three-body dynamics of p–p–\(\pmb{\Lambda}\) via correlation functions in ALICE at the LHC"

Abstract

The presence of hyperons in dense stellar matter is expected to soften the equation of state, giving rise to the so-called hyperon puzzle of neutron stars. Traditional calculations that lead to this conclusion rely primarily on two-body interactions when modeling hyperonic matter. Attempts to include the missing three-body contributions — based on available experimental constraints from \(\Lambda\)-hypernuclei — are limited by the insufficient precision of current data relative to theoretical developments. High-precision femtoscopic measurements can therefore substantially improve the description of the hyperon–nucleon–nucleon systems. During Run 2 at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the ALICE experiment reported the first measurement of femtoscopic correlations among p–p–\(\Lambda\) triplets produced in pp collisions. In this contribution, the preliminary Run 3 results for p–p–\(\Lambda\) correlations measured by ALICE in Pb–Pb collisions are presented. Comparing these measurements enables a differential characterization of the dynamics for different emission environments and to study the extent to which three-body forces are encoded in the p–p–\(\Lambda\) correlation function.

Cake: Anton

20.05.2026

docs.title: Sergei Golenev
docs.text:
Title: "HI-TREX: Compact, high resolution particle detection system for ISOLDE"

Abstract

HI-TREX is an advanced particle detection system designed for the HIE-ISOLDE facility at CERN, optimized for studying transfer reactions with radioactive ion beams. The system features thin double-sided silicon strip detectors (DSSSDs), high-resolution front-end electronics based on SKIROC ASICs, and a custom FPGA-based readout board integrated into the TRB data acquisition system. The detector performance has been evaluated in dedicated beam tests, including a recent experiment at the Cologne tandem accelerator with different targets and both proton and 16O beams. I will present the first data, highlighting the enhanced capabilities of HI-TREX and its potential to enable new research opportunities.

docs.title: Elias Sevdas
docs.text:
Title: "Proton Tracking for Quasi-Free Scattering Reactions with Pixel Detectors at R3B"

Abstract

The structure of exotic nuclei can be investigated through \((p, 2p)\) quasi-free scattering in inverse kinematics, in which a proton is knocked out of the projectile nucleus by a target proton. The R3B experiment (Reactions with Relativistic Radioactive Beams) allows for a kinematically complete reconstruction of these reactions. A key observable is the excitation energy (\(E_x\)) of the fragment. It is calculated from the beam information, the fragment mass, and the reconstructed momenta of the two outgoing protons.

For a precise measurement of \(E_x\), an accurate determination of the momentum vectors \(\vec{p}\) for both outgoing protons is essential. The proton trajectories will be measured using a new Target Recoil Tracker (TRT) in a two-barrel configuration with a barrel thickness of approximately 565 \(\mu m\). It is being considered to extend this setup with a third, significantly thinner 50 \(\mu m\) silicon barrel at the innermost position. The motivation is to improve the excitation energy resolution and to filter out the delta-electron background arising from the heavy ions traversing the target. This thesis investigates these improvements using GEANT4-based Monte Carlo simulations in the R3BRoot framework.

To study the delta-electron background, a simulation was performed with \({}^{238}\rm{U}\) ions at \(E_{\rm kin} = 400\) MeV/u. The fraction of unresolvable tracks in both barrel geometries was quantified. While in the two-barrel configuration 57% of all proton tracks could not be resolved from contamination by delta-electrons, two new methods developed in the framework of this thesis for the three-barrel configuration reduced this background contribution to 3.9%.

Regarding the excitation energy resolution, it was shown analytically and confirmed in simulations that among the reconstructed vertex coordinates, the uncertainty along the beam axis is the dominant contribution. A \((p, 2p)\) reaction with \({}^{132}\rm{Sn}\) at an energy of \(E_{\rm kin} = 400\) MeV/u was simulated for both configurations, and the excitation energy resolution was quantified. Because the three-barrel setup resolves the coordinate along the beam axis more precisely than the two-barrel setup, the full width at half maximum (FWHM) excitation energy resolution improves from \(\Delta E_x = 3.91\) MeV to \(\Delta E_x = 2.83\) MeV.

As a potential future improvement, a foil stack target was investigated to reduce the vertex uncertainty along the beam axis, improving the excitation energy resolution to \(\Delta E_x = 0.94\) MeV (FWHM) with the three-barrel setup.

29.04.2026

docs.title: Maximilian Korwieser
docs.text:
Title: "Normalizing-flow surrogate for femtoscopic source functions"

Abstract

Precise predictions of cosmic-ray antideuteron fluxes, a prime dark matter signature owing to their exceptionally low astrophysical background, require fully data-constrained femtoscopic source functions as input to state-of-the-art Wigner-function coalescence calculations, superseding the simplistic spherical momentum cut-off approach. Such sources remain poorly constrained, particularly in the ultra-low multiplicity regime most relevant for astrophysical applications. We present a normalizing-flow surrogate for femtoscopic source functions, trained on CECA (Common Emission in CATS, a state-of-the-art effective source model for small collision systems which encapsulates the effects of resonance production) simulations and simultaneously fit to 49 correlation functions double-differential in pair transverse mass \(m_T\) and event multiplicity. Exploiting the established \(m_T\)-multiplicity scaling of the emission source, higher-statistics event classes directly constrain the poorly populated low-multiplicity domain, delivering fully data-driven source functions without free parameters in the extrapolation. The surrogate is fast, differentiable, and accurate: closure tests confirm sub-percent emulation fidelity, and physics-driven validation recovers the correct \(m_T\) scaling and multiplicity dependence across all event classes. The resulting source-constrained B2 predictions are directly applicable to ongoing low-energy measurements at SMOG@LHCb, CBM@FAIR, and NA61/SHINE, and the framework is fully modular: any source model can be substituted or our B2 output ingested directly, with cosmic-ray propagation via standard transport codes the sole remaining step toward absolute antideuteron flux predictions for AMS-02 and GAPS.

Cake: Mrunmoy

28.01.2026

docs.title: Maximilian Korwieser
docs.text:
Title: "Fast Femtoscopic Source Modeling with Machine Learning: From Collisions to Cosmic Rays"

Abstract

Femtoscopic correlation measurements provide direct access to the space–time structure of particle emission in high-energy collisions. However, quantitative source studies are often limited by the high computational cost of evaluating realistic source models, making large-scale scans and systematic studies impractical. In this talk, I present a machine-learning surrogate model for femtoscopic sources that accurately emulates the full model calculation while reducing the evaluation time to effectively constant cost. Once trained, the surrogate enables fast and robust fits to arbitrarily large sets of correlation functions, opening new possibilities for high-statistics and multi-system analyses. Beyond acceleration, I discuss a task-transfer application: using the surrogate trained on heavy-ion data to estimate femtoscopic sources in very low-multiplicity and low-energy environments, where direct femtoscopic measurements are scarce. Machine learning is ideally suited to provide data-driven estimates in this regime. Such systems are relevant for understanding (anti-)nuclei production in cosmic rays, providing essential input for indirect dark matter searches by AMS and GAPS.

Title: "Analyzing (p,2p) and (p,pn) quasi-free scattering at the R3B Experiment"

Abstract

Quasi-free (proton and neutron knockout) reactions in inverse kinematics provide a valuable insight into the structure of nuclei far from stability. Providing kinematically complete measurements for incoming nuclei and outgoing reaction products, the R3B setup (Reactions with Relativistic Radioactive Beams) is ideal for studying such reactions.

Recently, the quasi-free scattering reaction \({}^{25}F(p,2p){}^{24}O\) has been measured with this setup in an attempt to understand the extension of the neutron drip line from \(Z=8\) nuclei to \(Z=9\) nuclei. This talk would highlight ongoing analysis of this experiment and energy reconstruction by the CALIFA calorimeter. In addition to this, approaches to identify neutron clusters in CALIFA, using Monte Carlo simulations will be discussed.

07.01.2026

docs.title: Georgios Mantzaridis
docs.text:
Title: "Probing the strangeness -2 sector with femtoscopy in ALICE with Run 3 data"

Abstract

The interaction between nucleons and hyperons in the double-strange sector play a critical role in determining the equation of state of dense baryonic matter, with implications for the structure of neutron stars. Traditionally, this sector has been studied by using hypernuclear spectroscopy. However, the scarce data on double strange hypernuclei have so far limited the extraction of precise information on the ΞN interaction and the nature of the hyothetical (quasi)boundstate in the ΛΛ system is still not fully setteled.

During the LHC Run 2 data taking, the ALICE Collaboration has provided rich information on the low-energy features of the Λ-Λ and p–Ξ− interactions by using the femtoscopy technique. The results were able to constrain (but not close) the parameterspace for the boundstate nature of in the ΛΛ and benchmark for the first time Lattice QCD calculations in the p–Ξ− system, providing experimental evidence of the attractive nature of the ΞN strong interaction. With the start of the LHC Run 3 data taking in 2022, ALICE has begun collecting significantly larger datasets, providing evidence of a pronounced signal at the opening of the Λ–Σ0 channel in the p–Ξ− correlation function. In this seminar we will discuss the current femtoscopic results in the strangeness -2 sector and present the preliminary result on p–Ξ− correlations measured in pp collisions from the first three years of the LHC Run 3. The measurement will be discussed by comparing the data to the correlation function calculated using the HAL-QCD potentials. Future prospects for extending these studies to the ΛΛ system will also be discussed. TBI finalize formatting of all math symbols

17.12.2025

docs.title: Marta Krawczyk
docs.text:
Title: "Study of Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors for ALICE 3"

Abstract

The ALICE collaboration plans to replace its experimental apparatus for the LHC Run 5 by an entirely new one, called ALICE 3. A key element of ALICE 3 will be the Vertex Detector (VD). To achieve the optimal pointing resolution, the detector will combine a \(10\mu\)m pixel pitch and a small distance of only 5 mm to the interaction point with minimal material budget. Furthermore, due to the proximity to the beam pipe as well as the expected interaction rate of about 25 MHz in proton-proton collisions, the pixel chips of the VD will need to resist a radiation load of approximately \(10^{16}\) 1 MeV \(n_{\rm eq}/{\rm cm}^2\) of Non-Ionizing Energy Loss (NIEL) and approximately 300 Mrad of Total-Ionizing Dose (TID). Moreover, a time resolution of 100 ns is targeted. These requirements constitute a significant challenge to CMOS pixel sensors planned to be employed for the VD.

This seminar talk describes the recently started pixel chip characterization work at the expected radiation levels and as a function of temperature using the Analog Pixel Test Structure (APTS). The key items of this presentation will be the temperature and radiation dependence of the gain and the operation range of the APTS circuitry.

Cake: Lukas

10.12.2025

docs.title: Tobias Jenegger
docs.text:
Title: "Advancements in Analysis & Instrumentation @ R3B"

Abstract

The R3B (Reactions with Relativistic Radioactive ion Beams) experiment, a key component of the NUSTAR collaboration at FAIR, enables high-precision investigations of radioactive nuclei in inverse kinematics through its large acceptance and complete kinematic reconstruction. As such it offers the unique possibility for understanding the dynamics of nuclear reactions under extreme conditions. This contribution presents recent progress in two central analysis fields: (i) benchmark measurements of the total interaction cross section of 12C + 12C for equation of-state studies at R3B, and (ii) quasi-free scattering reactions, including the pilot experiment fission via quasi-free scatttering \({}^{238}U(p, 2p)\) fission.

In addition, recent instrumental developments are highlighted, with a particular focus on the CALIFA calorimeter. The TUM group plays a leading role in its development and operation, contributing to hardware upgrades, software improvements, and the application of machine-learning techniques for enhanced cluster reconstruction. All these advancements contribute significantly to the promising experimental campaigns planned for the Early Science program at FAIR, scheduled to begin in 2028.

Cake: Georgios

26.11.2025

docs.title: Berkin Ulukutlu, Philipp Mann
docs.text:
Title: "Investigations with Bent BabyMOSS"

Abstract

The ALICE experiment at CERN is upgrading its Inner Tracking System (ITS) as part of the ITS3 project, which will replace the innermost tracking layers with wafer-scale, cylindrically bent Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors (MAPS). These new layers are placed closer to the collision point and have a lower material budget, leading to improved vertexing resolution. The use of bent silicon detectors at this scale is unprecedented and requires extensive R&D to address challenges related to the sensor geometry. In particular, it is important to understand how bending affects sensor behavior and performance. Earlier bent-chip studies focused on the ALPIDE sensor from ITS2 and the APTS chiplets from the MLR1 production of ITS3. In this talk, we present new bent-sensor studies conducted with the BabyMOSS chip, a 0.7-megapixel fully functional prototype fabricated using the 65 nm process. We describe the sensor design, the experimental setup developed for the bent-chip measurements, and provide an overview of results from laboratory and test beam studies, where a significant shift in the chip’s operating point was observed.

19.11.2025

docs.title: Maximilian Mahlein
docs.text:
Title: "First observation of (anti)deuteron formation from resonance-decay nucleons"

Abstract

The microscopic mechanism responsible for the formation of light (anti)(hyper)nuclei in hadron–hadron collisions remains one of the open questions in high-energy nuclear physics. While statistical hadronization and coalescence models both reproduce the measured yields, momentum spectra, and fluctuations in pp, p–A, and A–A collisions at ultra-relativistic energies, their fundamental physical assumptions are different, leading to model-dependent interpretations of the data.

In this work, new femtoscopy results on pion–deuteron correlations in pp collisions at \(\sqrt{s} = 13\) TeV, measured by the ALICE experiment, are presented. The correlation function directly probes the residual interaction between pions and nucleons originating from short-lived \(\Delta\) decays, followed by their coalescence into deuterons. This measurement provides, for the first time, a model-independent demonstration that (anti)deuteron production in ultra-relativistic pp collisions proceeds via nucleon coalescence. The results offer new constraints for the modeling of light- and heavy-nuclei formation in cosmic ray interactions and dark matter decay scenarios.

Cake: Anton

12.11.2025

docs.title: Seyed Farid Taghavi, Sebastian Wind
docs.text:
Title: "Collective Dynamics in OO and pp Collision Systems"

Abstract

In the first part, we discuss how collective behavior in high-energy collisions can be understood using a kinetic quasiparticle approach based on the Boltzmann equation. We introduce CoMBolt-ITA, a new tool for simulating relativistic systems in the relaxation time approximation, and apply it to recent OO collision data at the LHC to assess whether the system behaves more fluid-like or particle-like. In the second part, we compare source size predictions in pp collisions for free-streaming and ideal hydrodynamic evolution to highlight how spatial correlations reveal the degree of collectivity in small systems.

29.10.2025

docs.title: Wenya Wu
docs.text:
Title: "Flow in small systems"

Abstract

Quantum Chromodynamics predicts a transition from hadronic matter to a quark–gluon plasma (QGP) at extreme temperature and energy density, where quarks and gluons become deconfined. The QGP can be produced in high-energy heavy-ion collisions (HICs). Anisotropic flow coefficients, which characterize the collective motion of the medium, serve as key signatures of QGP formation. Measurements of transverse differential anisotropic flow reveal a baryon–meson grouping at intermediate transverse momentum, confirming QGP formation in HICs. Surprisingly, similar QGP-like features have been observed in high-multiplicity proton–proton and proton–lead collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The ALICE Collaboration has reported, for the first time, a clear baryon–meson flow grouping in these small systems. Hydrodynamic models with quark coalescence successfully describe these results, suggesting that collective partonic behavior emerge in small collision systems.

Cake: Valentina
